items.text: Medigap open enrollment is the six months after Part B starts. Buy then and health questions can't be used against you. Miss it, and medical underwriting can apply for life. Not connected with or endorsed by the U.S. government or the federal Medicare program.

Medigap open enrollment gets far less attention than the Medicare Annual Election Period, and it is arguably the more consequential deadline.

It runs once: the six months starting the month you are both 65 and enrolled in Part B. During that window, a Medigap insurer cannot use your health history to deny you a policy or charge you more for one.

After it closes, most states allow full medical underwriting. An insurer can decline you outright, or price the policy based on your health. Virginia is not one of the states with extra protections, so the six-month window matters here more than average.

We see this most often with clients who delayed Medigap because they felt fine, then developed a health condition a year or two later and found the door had closed.

If you are approaching 65, this is worth mapping out before the window opens, not after.

Approaching 65? Your one guaranteed window to buy a Medigap policy without health questions is the six months after you enroll in Part B. Miss it and insurers can use medical underwriting to deny coverage or raise the price for life. We map this window for you at no cost and explain what changes if you wait.
